simple.meaning: שַׁלִּיט (shallîyṭ) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “potent ; concretely, a prince or warrior.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 4 times across Genesis, Ecclesiastes, beginning at Genesis 42:6. Its contexts include family, city, land.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to שַׁלִּיט (H7989).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: שַׁלִּיט (shallîyṭ) / H7989 is traced through Genesis 42:6, Ecclesiastes 7:19, Ecclesiastes 8:8, Ecclesiastes 10:5 as a generated source-based concept entry.

definitions.short: potent ; concretely, a prince or warrior
definitions.usage: governor, mighty, that hath power, ruler.
definitions.full: H7989. shallit שַׁלִּיט adjective having mastery, domineering ; — 1 having mastery: שׁ אָדָם ׳אֵין בָּרוּחַ Eccl 8:8 ; elsewhere as substantive ׳הַשּׁ the ruler 10:5 , so (with עַלהָֿאָרֶץ ) Gen 42:6 (probably late substitution for original word of E); plural as substantive שַׁלִּיטִים Eccl 7:19 (specifically of Alexander's successors Perles Anal. 42 ). 2 domineering, imperious , feminine singular (Kö ii. 10. 201 ) שַׁלָּ֑טֶת זוֺנָה אִשָּׁה Ezek 16:30 (Jerusalem personified).

occurrences.englishText: Joseph was the governor over the land. It was he who sold to all the people of the land. Joseph’s brothers came, and bowed themselves down to him with their faces to the earth.
Wisdom is a strength to the wise man more than ten rulers who are in a city.

There is no man who has power over the spirit to contain the spirit; neither does he have power over the day of death. There is no discharge in war; neither shall wickedness deliver those who practice it.
There is an evil which I have seen under the sun, the sort of error which proceeds from the ruler.
